subject.title: Support Azure Foundry GPT Realtime Talk via gateway relay

question: Should Azure Foundry / Azure OpenAI Realtime Talk be owned by the existing `openai` realtime provider config, a new `azure-openai` realtime alias/provider, or the `microsoft-foundry` plugin surface?
rationale: Current main has partial Azure deployment bridge plumbing, but the requested first-class auth/config/diagnostics/docs path affects provider routing, security boundaries, and future Entra support.

options.title: Keep OpenAI-owned Azure bridge
options.body: Continue hardening `talk.realtime.providers.openai.azureEndpoint` and `azureDeployment` as the supported Azure Realtime Talk path.

options.title: Add Azure realtime alias/provider
options.body: Add an explicit `azure-openai` realtime provider or alias if maintainers want Azure routing separated from direct OpenAI Talk selection.

options.title: Move to Microsoft Foundry plugin
options.body: Make the Foundry plugin own Realtime Talk only if its provider/auth hooks grow a realtime voice contract.

recommendation.title: Keep OpenAI-owned Azure bridge
recommendation.body: Continue hardening `talk.realtime.providers.openai.azureEndpoint` and `azureDeployment` as the supported Azure Realtime Talk path.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current code-history signal is the merged GA realtime bridge work in the OpenAI provider and Talk docs.
